summary: Provide a specialist bridge from GPU software behavior to an open GPU RTL implementation and verification workflow.
outcomes: Trace fetch, scheduling, execution and memory interfaces in a small open design.
State and test a microarchitectural invariant with a bounded RTL experiment.
sequence: Introduce Boolean logic, sequential state and clocked interfaces before RTL syntax.
Trace a tiny SIMT instruction through an open GPU block diagram.
Explain hazards, scoreboards, divergence and memory requests.
Add a small module change with simulation and assertions.
Discuss synthesis, timing, area, power and the limits of an FPGA prototype.

visual.question: Why must this instruction wait before it can issue?
visual.interaction: Step dependencies and memory responses; highlight scoreboard hazards.

practice.task: Analyze or modify one bounded open-source GPU module.
practice.success: Verification covers the stated invariant and regression cases; no claim of tapeout-ready ASIC design.
